pick.headline: Bomb destroys Israeli military headquarters in Tyre
pick.summary: On 11 November 1982 a car bomb destroyed the Israeli military government headquarters in Tyre, southern Lebanon, killing scores of Israeli soldiers and border police and Lebanese prisoners.
pick.significance: Later attributed to the forerunners of Hizballah, it was one of the first suicide bombings of the Lebanon war, a tactic used against the US Embassy and Marines in Beirut in 1983.
pick.fbis: FBIS's Middle East review of 12 November 1982 reported, from Jerusalem radio, that an explosion had devastated the Israeli military headquarters in Tyre early on 11 November, killing at least 26.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: Middle East & Africa, Vol. V No. 219, 12 November 1982
evidence.snippet: DAILY REPORT MIDDLE EAST AND SOUTH ASTA REVIEW 12 NOVEMBER L982 Lebanon Tyre Explosion -- An explosion devastated the Israeli military headquarters in Tyre early on 11 November, killing at least 26 people and wounding many others, Jerusalem radio reported. alternates.headline: Moscow announces the death of Leonid Brezhnev
alternates.summary: On 11 November 1982 Soviet radio and television announced that Leonid Brezhnev had died the previous morning.
alternates.significance: Brezhnev had led the USSR since 1964. His death opened a period of rapid succession: Andropov, then Chernenko, then Gorbachev.
alternates.fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of 12 November 1982 listed reaction across the bloc: Bucharest radio announcing Brezhnev's death, Poland paying homage, and Yugoslav condolences.

alternates.headline: FMLN launches its offensive on San Salvador
alternates.summary: On 11 November 1989 El Salvador's FMLN guerrillas launched their largest offensive of the war, fighting into San Salvador itself.
alternates.significance: The offensive showed that neither side could win militarily and that US aid had not defeated the insurgency, pushing both towards the UN-brokered negotiations that ended the war in 1992.
alternates.fbis: The Latin America report of 13 November 1989 carried Salvadoran radio accounts of rebel incursions in the capital, including FMLN urban commandos attacking the bodyguards of the Legislative Assembly president.
